title: Kerr comb
title_note: Read from the arXiv preprint (arXiv:0708.0611v1, 2007-08-04) of Del'Haye et al., Nature 450, 1214 (2007); page numbers are arXiv pages. Name: the paper calls the bright, equally spaced sidebands "Kerr combs" (p.2); it does not use the later word "microcomb". It calls the approach "entirely novel" (abstract) and makes no "first" claim. The fabrication steps are those of the toroid process the paper cites (Armani et al., Nature 2003); the paper itself prints no process values. The traced drawing is FIG. 2A of the same group's patent US 7,982,944 (public domain).
tagline: A CW laser and a silica toroid make an equidistant frequency comb.

parts.name: Silicon chip
parts.role: Silicon substrate that carries the toroid
parts.detail: The paper: "silica toroidal microcavities[13] on a silicon chip" (p.2); Fig. 1C: "Scanning electron microscope image of a toroid microcavity on a silicon chip". The cited process starts from "a (100) prime grade silicon substrate" (Armani et al., Nature 2003, p.925). XeF_{2} etching lowers the surface around the pillar; the SEM shows the etched silicon floor and pillar with a rough, grainy texture. Chip size and thickness are not given: a square patch is drawn, cut off at the edges.

parts.name: Photoresist disk
parts.role: Disk-shaped resist pad that masks the oxide etch
parts.detail: Cited process: "photolithography is performed to create disk-shaped photo-resist pads (160 µm in diameter)"; "An additional bake follows in order to reflow the photo-resist, smoothing the edges"; the pads mask the oxide "during immersion in buffered HF solution at room temperature"; "Acetone is then used to remove residual photo-resist" (Armani et al., Nature 2003, p.925-926). That paper gives 160 µm pads for the process in general; its Fig. 2 example toroid is 120 µm (94 and 90 µm toroids are also shown) and it does not link a pad size to a toroid size. The pad for the 75 µm comb toroid is not stated: drawn 100 µm (75 µm x 160 / 120, the cited pad size over the example toroid size), an assumption. Resist colour is a rendering choice.

parts.name: XeF₂ gas
parts.role: Etches silicon isotropically; leaves silica untouched
parts.detail: Cited process: "exposure to XeF_{2} gas at 3 torr. XeF_{2} was specifically chosen for the purpose of isotropic selective removal of silicon. As a result, the edges of the SiO_{2} disks are equally undercut, leaving circular silicon pillars supporting larger SiO_{2} disks." Removing silicon under the periphery is "required to inhibit power leakage into the substrate" (Armani et al., Nature 2003, p.926). Drawn as a faint haze: the gas colour is a rendering choice.

parts.name: Silicon pillar
parts.role: Silicon post left by the undercut; holds the disk
parts.detail: Isotropic XeF_{2} etching leaves "circular silicon pillars supporting larger SiO_{2} disks"; during the laser reflow "The silicon pillar therefore remains significantly cooler and physically unaffected", acting as a heat sink, because silicon absorbs far less at 10.6 µm and "is 100 times more thermally conductive than silica" (Armani et al., Nature 2003, p.926). Shape read from the comb paper's SEM (Fig. 1C): a concave pillar, narrowest under the disk and flaring to the floor. That SEM shows a toroid about 62 µm across by its 30 µm scale bar, so it is not identified as the 75 µm comb device; pillar sizes here are estimates from it.

parts.name: CO₂ laser beam
parts.role: Surface-normal 10.6 µm beam that melts the disk rim
parts.detail: Cited process: "An undercut SiO_{2} disk is surface-normal-irradiated using a CO_{2} laser (10.6-µm wavelength)"; "The beam intensity profile follows an approximately gaussian distribution and is focused to a circular spot approximately 200 µm in diameter"; intensity "typically 100 MW m^{-2} during reflow". Silica's absorption near 10.6 µm rises strongly with temperature ("strong temperature dependence of the silica optical extinction coefficient near 10.6 µm") and the undercut rim is thermally isolated, while silicon has "a far weaker optical absorption at 10.6 µm"; so "melting of the disk occurs along the periphery, and significantly not over the silicon pillar". The beam is infrared and invisible: its colour here is illustrative (Armani et al., Nature 2003, p.926).

parts.name: Silica toroid
parts.role: Whispering-gallery microresonator; light circulates in the rim
parts.detail: Reflow is self-limiting: "As the disk diameter shrinks, the effective cross-section available to absorb laser power decreases and shrinkage is observed to terminate when a toroid-like silica structure has formed"; surface tension "both smoothes the surface and collapses the silica disk to a toroid shape" (Armani et al., Nature 2003, p.926). The comb paper uses "ultra-high-Q monolithic microresonators in the form of silica toroidal microcavities[13] on a silicon chip, which possess giant photon storage times (τ) i.e. ultra-high quality factors (Q = 2πντ > 10^{8}) and small mode volumes" (p.2). Fig. 1A device: 75 µm diameter. Whether 75 µm is the outer or the centre-line diameter is not stated: drawn as the outer diameter. Rim (minor) diameter about 5 µm from the SEM sample (Fig. 1C); the cited process reports "various radii (80-120 µm) and tori thickness (5-10 µm)" and a 7 µm thick rim on its 120 µm example. A thin silica membrane spans from the pillar to the rim (SEM).

parts.name: Tapered fiber
parts.role: Stretched fiber; its thin waist couples light in and out
parts.detail: The paper: "Highly efficient coupling is achieved using tapered optical fibers[25]" (p.2); Fig. 2 caption: the laser is "coupled to an ultra-high-Q monolithic microresonator in a nitrogen environment via a tapered fiber". The comb light is "outcoupled from the microresonator back to the tapered fiber" (SI p.6-7). Cited toroid paper: tapers are made by "stretching a standard optical fibre (SMF-28), which has been heated using a hydrogen flame"; "Taper waist diameters are typically several micrometres"; "Proper alignment required the taper axis to reside in the equatorial plane of the toroidal cavity"; gaps "of the order of hundreds of nanometres" (Armani et al., Nature 2003, p.926). Waist size, gap and coupling regime of the Fig. 1A measurement are not stated. The taper transitions and the full fiber run off the frame.

parts.name: Signal and idler
parts.role: First sidebands born from two pump photons
parts.detail: Four-wave mixing "among two pump photons (frequency ν_{P}) with a signal (ν_{S}) and idler photon (ν_{I}) and results in the emergence of (phase coherent) signal and idler sidebands from the vacuum fluctuations at the expense of the pump field" (p.1). Energy conservation: hν_{I} + hν_{S} = 2hν_{P}, so the sidebands sit symmetrically about the pump. Momentum conservation holds intrinsically for whispering-gallery modes: two pump photons in mode N go to modes N-ΔN and N+ΔN (p.1). Colours follow Fig. 1B: blue for the higher mode (m+1), pink for the lower (m-1).
parts.quote: results in the emergence of (phase coherent) signal and idler sidebands from the vacuum fluctuations at the expense of the pump field
parts.locator: Del'Haye et al., arXiv:0708.0611 (2007), p.1 col. 1-2; Fig. 1B (p.2)

geometry.note: colours after Fig. 1B arrows; illustrative for infrared light

parts.name: Kerr comb
parts.role: Cascaded sidebands, equally spaced by the free spectral range
parts.detail: Signal and idler "interact among each other and produce higher order sidebands" by non-degenerate four-wave mixing, which transfers the pump-to-sideband spacing exactly to all higher sidebands, "e.g. ν_{S2} = ν_{P} + ν_{S} - ν_{I} = ν_{P} - 2Δν" (p.1). Fig. 1A: emission "spaced by the cavity free spectral range"; the figure labels the spacing "Δλ ≈ 7 nm". 49 lines resolved in Fig. 1A from 1360 to 1726 nm (digitized); their positions fit one frequency spacing of 0.975 THz (derived from the printed axis; 7.8 nm at the pump). Another sample gave "more than 70 parametric modes" over nearly 500 nm with 130 mW launched (Fig. 1 inset); the largest samples (190 µm) gave 380 nm wide combs of 134 modes spaced by 375 GHz (p.2); the SI Fig. 5 caption gives that comb as a 177 µm toroid with more than 134 lines (SI p.6). The outward cascade drawn here shows the mechanism, not a measured time sequence.
parts.quote: the initially generated signal and idler sidebands can interact among each other and produce higher order sidebands (cf. Fig. 1) by non-degenerate four-wave mixing (FWM)
parts.locator: Del'Haye et al., arXiv:0708.0611 (2007), p.1 col. 2; Fig. 1 caption (p.2)

parts.name: Fiber-laser reference comb
parts.role: 100 MHz mode-locked fiber comb used as the frequency ruler
parts.detail: The paper: "a fiber-laser based optical frequency comb[26] from Menlo Systems (termed "reference comb" ...) as a reference grid whose repetition rate is f_{rep} = 100 MHz"; beat notes are recorded in beat note detection units (polarizing optics plus a grating). chapters.line: One CW laser and one silica microresonator make many equidistant lines.
chapters.action: finished toroid on its pillar over the chip, taper beside it, slow orbit; then fade back to the bare chip

chapters.line: Thermal oxide on silicon, patterned into disks with resist and acid.
chapters.action: oxide film appears on the chip; resist disk appears; buffered-HF etch removes the oxide outside the disk; resist lifts off

chapters.line: Xenon difluoride gas etches silicon; a pillar is left holding the disk.
chapters.action: haze over the chip; silicon floor drops from the disk underside to y = 0 and recedes under the disk edge until the concave pillar remains; silica disk unchanged

chapters.line: A CO_{2} laser melts the rim; surface tension forms a torus.
chapters.action: wide beam from above covers the disk; the edge glows (pillar region stays cool); the disk diameter shrinks from 100 to 75 µm while the rim thickens into the torus; shrinking stops by itself; beam off

chapters.line: A smooth silica rim that stores light for a long time.
chapters.action: camera circles the finished toroid; diameter label

chapters.line: A stretched fiber waist slides in beside the rim, in its plane.
chapters.action: taper enters from the side at rim height (equatorial plane), stops just short of the rim; never from above

chapters.line: Infrared laser light couples into the rim and circulates.
chapters.action: pump light runs +x along the taper from the laser box; part couples into the rim and circulates in the same sense as the taper light at the coupling point; transmitted pump continues to +x

chapters.line: Two pump photons become one signal photon and one idler photon.
chapters.action: inside the circulating pump, a blue and a pink sideband appear together (symmetric about the pump); they couple out into the taper and run +x with the pump

chapters.line: Sidebands mix again; lines cascade, spaced by the free spectral range.
chapters.action: more sideband colours appear outward from the pump in step with the plot (pump first, then nearest lines, then outer); comb light leaves the taper toward the analyzer box; model in the left half

chapters.line: Counted against a fiber-laser reference comb, the spacing holds to millihertz.
chapters.action: reference comb box beside the output; comb keeps circulating; histogram assembles; model in the left half
